about: How each AI model maker says to write prompts, from their own guides. lib/prompts.js reads this to shape every prompt per model. maxChars is the longest prompt we build for that model: the maker's documented cap where one is published (basis: documented), else our own cap kept well under any limit seen (basis: house).

higgsfield.label: Higgsfield
notes: Pick the camera move as a preset in Higgsfield (Dolly In, 360 Orbit, Crane Up, FPV Drone and more). The preset does the move; the words say what the subject does while it happens.
Say the speed and where the shot starts and ends, or results drift between tries.
Pick a starting photo that suits the move: subject centered for orbits, dolly and zooms, a wide scene for FPV and handheld, a close-up for POV.
Change one thing at a time between tries: the move, then the lens, then the depth of field.
higgsfield.fromImage: The photo is the first frame. Write what the subject does and how fast; the preset handles the camera.

kling.label: Kling
kling.style: one or two sentences, subject first
kling.maxCharsBasis: documented (Kling API limits as published in the ComfyUI Kling nodes: 2500 text to video, 500 image to video)
kling.negativeDefault: blurry, warped hands, extra fingers, distorted face, flicker, garbled text, watermark, low quality
notes: Kling reads subject, subject movement, scene, then camera language, lighting and atmosphere.
Use one main camera move per shot and say its speed: slow, stable pan left, no sudden motion.
Plain camera words beat vague ones: slow dolly in, pull back, orbit slowly, static camera.
Describe a start and end frame for reveals: start on a close-up of the label, then pull back.
Kling takes a separate negative prompt for things to keep out.
kling.fromImage: Keep the subject description short and steady; spend the words on what moves and how the camera moves.

veo.label: Google Veo
veo.negativeDefault: blurry footage, warped hands, distorted faces, on-screen text, watermark
notes: Google's formula: cinematography, then subject, action, context, then style and ambiance.
Veo makes sound. Write dialogue in quotes after who says it, sound effects after SFX:, and background sound after Ambient noise:.
Describe what you want rather than what to leave out: a quiet street with no cars reads better than no cars.
Length, resolution and shape are settings, not prompt words: 4, 6 or 8 seconds, 16:9 or 9:16.
Keep one speaker per clip: one voice lip-syncs far more reliably than two.
veo.fromImage: Veo animates a start image, or a start and end frame: describe the change between them and the sound.

runway.label: Runway
runway.style: [camera] shot of [subject] [action] in [setting]; with a photo: The camera [move] as the subject [action].
runway.maxCharsBasis: documented (Runway API promptText up to 1,000 characters)
notes: Runway's template: [camera] shot of [subject] [action] in [environment], then any supporting detail.
Positive words only. Describe what you want to see; negative phrasing can backfire.
Start simple and add one detail at a time between tries.
If you see unwanted cuts, try the longer length or add: continuous, seamless shot.
For no camera movement: the locked-off camera remains perfectly still.
runway.fromImage: With a photo, write almost only about motion: The camera [move] as the subject [action]. Describing what the photo already shows can reduce motion.

luma.label: Luma Ray
luma.style: about 100 words or fewer, present tense, action first
notes: Order: main subject, action, details, scene, style, camera move.
Positive only: Luma treats negative prompting as counterproductive.
Name one specific move (dolly forward, slow pan right, camera circles slowly) and add a secondary motion like dust, fabric or reflections.
Present tense, about 100 words. Skip filler like hyper-realistic.
A 5 second clip holds one clear action; 10 seconds can hold a beginning, middle and end.
luma.fromImage: Use your photo as the start keyframe (or end keyframe) and write the motion that happens from it.

sora.label: Sora-style
sora.style: a short scene paragraph, then Cinematography, Actions in beats, and Dialogue blocks
notes: Write the scene in plain prose, then a Cinematography line (shot and mood), then the actions as timed beats.
One camera move, one subject action and one lighting recipe per shot.
Shorter clips follow the prompt more closely: two 4 second clips often beat one 8 second clip.
Dialogue goes in its own block and stays brief: one or two short lines in 4 seconds.
Leave out what doesn't matter; the model fills it in. Length and size are settings, not prompt words.
sora.fromImage: The image anchors the first frame; write what happens next.

flux.label: FLUX
flux.maxCharsBasis: house (FLUX guide: 30 to 80 words is usually ideal)
notes: FLUX weighs early words most: lead with the subject, then the action, style and context.
No negative prompts. Describe the opposite: empty instead of no people, brightly lit instead of not dark.
Put any words for the image in quotes and say where they go, how big and what color.
Attach each hex color to one object: a backdrop in color #1F6FEB.
Name a camera, lens, aperture or film look for a photo feel instead of professional photo.

imagen.label: Imagen and Gemini image
imagen.style: subject, context, style; full sentences for Gemini image
imagen.negativeDefault: blurry, distorted hands, extra fingers, watermark, cluttered background
notes: Build from subject, context and background, then style. Add detail one round at a time.
Keep words in the image to 25 characters or fewer, and no more than three short phrases.
A negative prompt lists things plainly (wall, frame), without no or don't.
Photo words that work: close-up, aerial, from below, natural or dramatic light, bokeh, 35mm, 50mm, macro, wide angle.
On the Gemini API, Imagen has given way to Gemini image (Nano Banana): the same prompts work, written as full sentences.

general: Describe motion, not the picture, when you animate a photo.
One camera move and one main action per shot.
Never put a real person's name or another company's logo in a prompt.
UGC-style shots are your own demo or a creator you hire who says they were paid. Never script a customer review.
